directOfficialCannabisLawLinks.note: Albania independently reaches proposal-only YELLOW. Current Criminal Code Article 283 expressly excludes personal use and small doses from that criminal offence, and a current Supreme Court bulletin applies Article 283/1 to cannabis sativa. This is affirmative limited non-criminal cannabis evidence, not Green adult-use. Current Law 61/2023 Article 5 expressly prohibits domestic acquisition and consumption of medical cannabis products; current NACC FAQ confirms general use is not legalised and Law 61 output is exclusively for export. The former RED proposal is therefore too broad because it erased the direct narrow personal-use exclusion. SSOT, map, runtime, production and deployment unchanged.

directOfficialCannabisLawLinks.note: Independent proposal-only conclusion: YELLOW. independentTruth.conclusion: AQ is a composite Antarctic Treaty area. The current Treaty Secretariat page confirms Party-specific domestic implementation and competent authorities, but no single territorial cannabis possession, adult-use, medical-patient or enforcement regime applies to whole Antarctica. Treaty permitting and international cannabis-control context cannot substitute for territorial law. AQ remains UNKNOWN and unpainted.

Neither source is cannabis-law evidence and neither extends any Party law to all Antarctica. Accordingly AQ remains proposal-only UNKNOWN and unpainted for the explicit reason NO_UNITARY_APPLICABLE_REGIME. It is neither RED by absence nor YELLOW/GREEN by analogy.

rows.differenceDescription: Current map, popup, API, SEO, SSOT and wiki-truth records remain comparison-only inputs and were not used to derive the no-unitary-regime conclusion. Повторный аудит: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает AQ жёлтым и не выдаёт Antarctica за единое государство или единый уголовный кодекс. Официальная страница Antarctic Treaty Secretariat прямо говорит, что Parties реализуют Treaty и Environment Protocol через собственные national legislations, а посетители получают разрешения у соответствующих National Competent Authorities. Визуально проверенный Article VIII самого Antarctic Treaty закрепляет национальную юрисдикцию для observers, exchanged scientific personnel и сопровождающего персонала, а споры о юрисдикции для иных случаев решаются консультациями сторон. Одновременно действующий Annex II Article 4 устанавливает общий для Antarctic Treaty area материальный минимум: никакой не местный живой организм нельзя вводить на сушу, ледовые шельфы или в воду без permit; разрешения допускают cultivated plants и reproductive propagules только для controlled use, а living organisms — для controlled experimental use, после чего их требуется удалить или обезвредить. Официальный UNODC Single Convention визуально определяет Cannabis, Cannabis plant и Cannabis resin и показывает международный medical/scientific-only контроль, а актуальный INCB Yellow List визуально включает cannabis и cannabis resin/extracts/tinctures в Schedule I; эти документы используются как прямой cannabis-идентификатор и общий международный контекст, а не как выдуманный единый AQ criminal code. Поэтому для whole-Antarctica нет общего recreational legal market или общего права на выращивание: введение живого cannabis plant permit-only, а медицинское/научное обращение и иные possession/use вопросы зависят от национальной юрисдикции и компетентного органа. В трёхцветной модели такой ограниченный условный режим — жёлтый. Не утверждается, что все национальные режимы одинаковы, что найден единый AQ possession offence, что существует AQ patient programme или что конкретный cannabis medicine доступен. Статус SSOT не изменён.

rows.differenceDescription: UN-hosted material records an NGO description of Bir Tawil as unclaimed territory, while the UN Law of the Sea Bulletin preserves Egypt/Sudan boundary positions; neither is a BRT lawmaker, territorial cannabis statute, or extension rule. Egypt and Sudan access-state law does not become law of BRT merely because those states border the area. The general resolver requires direct territorial applicability before a colour may be derived. BRT remains UNKNOWN for NO_UNITARY_APPLICABLE_REGIME. Повторный аудит: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает BRT жёлтым, не изобретая государство, территориальный уголовный кодекс или CannabisLawPage Bir Tawil. В отчёте Генерального секретаря ООН A/80/304 формулировка unclaimed territory приведена в разделе вкладов неправительственных организаций: это официально опубликованное negative/context evidence, но не обязательное юридическое решение ООН. Официальные заявления Egypt и Sudan, опубликованные в UN Law of the Sea Bulletin No. 94, визуально показывают несовместимые пограничные позиции: Egypt считает международной границей 22-ю параллель и относит территории к югу от неё к Sudan, тогда как Sudan заявляет Hala'ib к северу от 22-й параллели по унаследованной границе. Ни одна из просмотренных государственных веток не публикует орган Bir Tawil, территориальный cannabis-law, полицию, суд или patient programme; частные micronation-декларации поэтому отвергнуты. Для обязательного трёхцветного отображения применяется явно обозначенный operational-access fallback, а не территориальный закон: физический сухопутный доступ возможен только через Egypt или Sudan, и обе реальные CannabisLawPage просмотрены глазами. Egypt EDA публикует Law No. 182/1960 и актуальный индекс поправок до 2020 года; закон помещает Cannabis sativa/Indian hemp в запрещённые к выращиванию растения, запрещает неразрешённые cultivation, import, possession и trade, допускает только лицензируемые medical/scientific операции и предусматривает строгие наказания. Sudan Judiciary на действующем официальном сайте в 2026 году продолжает применять Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act 1994 и его таблицы, включая дела о hashish; визуально проверенная копия UNODC Legal Library определяет hashish как Indian hemp, перечисляет cannabis, cannabis resin и tetrahydrocannabinols, запрещает import, production, possession, transport и trade, оставляя только minister-authorized medical/scientific purposes и строгие уголовные наказания. Поэтому доказанного общего recreational legal market нет, а допустимость ограничена разрешительными медицинскими/научными режимами двух единственных сухопутных access states. В трёхцветной модели это жёлтый: зелёный ложно утверждал бы доказанную легальность, красный ложно приписал бы BRT собственный запрет. Enforcement строг на маршрутах Egypt/Sudan, но отдельной BRT enforcement authority нет. Вывод не распространяет автоматически суверенитет Egypt или Sudan на Bir Tawil, не создаёт BRT patient programme и не меняет статус SSOT.

independentTruth.conclusion: Official AGEMED evidence proves an individual exceptional and exclusive cannabis-oil compassionate-use import authorisation under Ley 913 art. 18(II), with treating-doctor supervision and an administrative pre-licence. This establishes a special-permit cannabis route only. It does not prove a general patient-eligibility rule, current clinician-certification route, routine licensed pharmacy/dispensary supply or operational patient programme; GREEN is therefore prohibited.

rows.differenceDescription: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает BV красным без автоматического переноса всего материкового медицинского режима Norway. Bilandsloven визуально подтверждает норвежский суверенитет над Bouvetøya и прямо распространяет на biland норвежское уголовное право. Официальный government analysis Prop. 69 L подтверждает ту же норму: private law, criminal law и law of procedure действуют на bilandene, а специальное законодательство и подзаконные акты требуют отдельного основания. Действующий правительственный cannabis-раздел визуально связывает cannabis с уголовными §§231 и 162: оборот, передача, пересылка, use и possession вне медицинских/научных целей незаконны. Narkotikaforskriften визуально называет Cannabis и Cannabisharpiks и показывает запрет §5, а Penal Code устанавливает строгие сроки за narcotics offences. Но отдельного акта, распространяющего на Bouvetøya материковый patient-access режим legemiddelloven/DMP, не найдено, и национальная medical-cannabis страница не выдаётся за BV-specific право. Поэтому минимально доказанный территориальный режим: recreational запрещён, criminal enforcement строгий, подтверждённого BV medical-cannabis patient pathway нет. В трёхцветной модели это красный; вывод не утверждает, что на необитаемом острове существует абсолютный запрет любой медицинской помощи.

Article 134 penalizes contravention of regulatory provisions, not cannabis conduct by itself. The INCB Yellow List visibly names cannabis in the international Schedule I, but is international context, not evidence of a current Chadian cannabis regime. Fresh searches of the Chad Official Gazette, Presidency, Health Ministry and decree/order terms found no applicable current cannabis-specific implementing instrument. The page visibly states that cultivation of plants of the Cannabis genus is prohibited, prohibits hemp extract and tincture handling, and prohibits hemp, hemp resin and usual hemp-resin preparations such as hashish, esrar, chiras and djamba for import/export and possession/presence/use. Article 7 visibly contains licensed and professional medical-purpose exceptions. The official Ministry of Health, Environment and Nature application form under the Opium Ordinance was also rendered and visually reviewed; it expressly applies to licences to cultivate, produce and/or manufacture cannabis or cannabis material, including cannabis/cannabis resin/cannabis oil for supply to patients or research, and lists licence categories for import, export, transit, cultivation, processing/manufacturing, selling, delivery, transport and possession of cannabis/cannabis oil/resin. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported, but project medical=NONE is contradicted by the official medicinal cannabis/research licensing pathway. The reviewed material supports at least LIMITED medical/research licensing scope, not a broad recreational allowance.

rows.differenceDescription: Journal Officiel RDC publication-copy PDFs for Arrêté 038/2022, Arrêté 039/2022 and the Arrêté 040/2022 fees annex were downloaded, rendered and visually reviewed. Arrêté 038 is visibly identified as J.O.RDC., 6 mars 2023, n° spécial, col. 35 and fixes exploitation conditions for narcotics and psychotropic substances for medical and scientific purposes. Article 2 visibly states exploitation is authorized only and exclusively for medical and scientific purposes, while culture, production, possession, use and commercialization for other purposes remain strictly prohibited. Article 3 visibly defines cannabis, cannabis for medical purposes, cannabis for scientific purposes, cannabis plant and cannabis resin. Articles 96-119 visibly create a medical/scientific cannabis chapter with authorization for cannabis cultivation and production, THC limits for medical cultivation, no THC limit for scientific cannabis, import/export/transport/control rules and sanction/withdrawal triggers for illegal or recreational use. Arrêté 039 visibly creates the CMPC for medical and scientific cannabis activities, and the fees annex visibly lists licences, taxes and fines for cannabis activities. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported outside the authorized framework, but project medical=NONE is contradicted by the visually reviewed official-publication material showing a licensed medical/scientific cannabis framework. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: No separate French Guiana-issued cannabis law page was found or treated as direct territorial law. Instead, the official scope and cannabis evidence was visually reviewed as French national law/public-health material applicable to Guyane. The Vie-publique official overseas territories page visibly marks Guyane as a DROM and states that DROM are governed by Article 73 / legislative identity, meaning national laws and regulations apply there as of right; it also says Guyane adopted the single territorial collectivity status while remaining in the DROM category. The Drogues.gouv official page visibly explains that a substance listed as a narcotic cannot be freely used, produced, manufactured, imported, exported, transported, possessed, offered or sold, and that French narcotics law represses illicit use and trafficking. The Service-public official cannabis therapeutique page visibly states the medical cannabis experiment ended on 31 December 2024, a transition period was initiated for patients still under treatment, initially until 31 March 2026 and extended until 3 months after the forthcoming HAS opinion publication, and no new patient can enter since 27 March 2024. The ANSM patient page visibly confirms only patients included before 27 March 2024 can continue prescriptions and dispensing of cannabis-based medicines during the transition, while the ANSM professional page visibly lists the five therapeutic indications, trained prescriber/pharmacist requirements, secured prescriptions/storage for THC above 0.3 percent, and that flower initiation has stopped. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=LIMITED and enforcement=STRICT are supported under this national-DROM scope. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: French Polynesia is not a DROM/article 73 territory, so the French Guiana national-law scope shortcut was not reused. A 15 July 2025 official Polynesie francaise Ministry of Health / ARASS note, published on service-public.pf under the DGAE path, was downloaded and visually rendered. Page 1 visibly identifies Polynesie francaise and the Ministry of Health / ARASS, states the object as products of cannabis authorized in French Polynesia and their import conditions / professional obligations, and cites Loi du pays n 2024-19 of 23 August 2024 and Arrete n 118 CM of 6 February 2025 regulating activities relating to cannabis without narcotic properties and medicines containing cannabis or cannabinoids. Page 2 visibly states that only identified categories of cannabis products can be authorized, that they must have delta-9-THC less than or equal to 0.30 percent, comply with labeling/presentation and biosecurity rules, and that products failing all conditions are not authorized. It lists allowed categories such as food products from cannabis seeds or dried leaves for aqueous infusions, supplements from cannabis seed/oil/powder without narcotic properties, cosmetics with non-narcotic cannabinoids such as CBD, tobacco products from non-narcotic cannabis plant parts, bird-feed cannabis seeds, and cannabis-fibre products; it also says local production is authorized subject to mandatory declarations. Page 3 visibly maps cannabis/cannabinoid product categories to competent administrations, including ARASS for medicines and therapeutic oils, DGAE for foods/cosmetics/fibre products, Direction de la sante and biosecurity/customs involvement. Page 4 visibly states import conditions and professional obligations, including that Arrete 118 CM regulates manufacturing, packaging and labeling of cannabis products and that manufacturers/packagers must declare to DGAE. The official Direction de la sante Drogues et Addictions page was opened live with HTTP 200, the 'Ce que dit la loi' accordion was expanded, and the screenshot visibly states that consuming, planting, manufacturing, transporting, giving, selling, importing or exporting drugs such as pakalolo are prohibited by law with arrests/prosecutions/sanctions. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT remain supported, but project medical=NONE is not aligned with the visually verified official 2024/2025 framework for cannabis/cannabinoid medicines and non-narcotic cannabis products. No project status SSOT was changed. Повторный аудит: Официальная записка 2025 визуально перечисляет Loi du pays 2024-19 и условия для cannabis/cannabinoid products и лекарств во French Polynesia.

rows.differenceDescription: Independent recheck: Guatemala Decreto 48-92 Article 2 defines drugs generally, including plants or plant parts from which drugs can be extracted and substances under treaties mandatory in Guatemala. Article 3 permits strictly necessary drug activities by legally empowered persons for medical treatment, analyses, research and medicine manufacture, with prescription required for retail sale. Articles 36-39 criminalise unauthorised activity for the same general drug category. The MSPAS-published treaty pages name cannabis but state that each Party must criminalise conduct in its domestic law; they are international context, not a domestic cannabis product, patient or conduct rule. Fresh current MSPAS pages prove an operating generic controlled-substance administration system (company registration, authorised narcotic prescriptions, quotas and import forms), but no cannabis-specific product registration, patient eligibility, dispensing route or cannabis-specific permit was located. The 2026 MSPAS alert title naming illegal cannabis product manufacture/commercialisation was identified, but its scanned text was not readable in this audit environment and is not used as a legal conclusion. Thus the former Yellow/strict-negative inference mixed generic domestic terms, generic operational procedures and treaty text. GT remains proposal-only UNKNOWN; current map RED and SSOT remain unchanged.

The MOHA consolidated Cap. 10:10 PDF was downloaded and rendered: page 8 visibly defines cannabis as any plant of the genus Cannabis and cannabis resin as separated resin from cannabis; page 17 visibly states any person who has in possession any narcotic is liable to fine plus imprisonment; page 87 visibly states a court may treat possession of cannabis not exceeding five grams for personal consumption as a special reason. legalInterpretation.notes: A directly indexed Haiti government-hosted cannabis-law page was not found in this pass. The reviewed sources are UNODC CLD official legal-database PDFs for Haiti, not Haiti government-hosted pages, so the host caveat must remain visible. The 2001 Loi relative au contrôle et à la répression du trafic illicite de la drogue PDF was downloaded, rendered and visually inspected. Page 1 visibly identifies the law, cites the Code pénal, Code d'instruction criminelle, the 1975 decree on narcotics, and states that the Executive proposed and the legislative body voted the law. Page 3 visibly defines production as collecting opium, coca leaf, cannabis and cannabis resin from the plants that provide them, defines cannabis resin, and defines controlled substances/drogues. Page 5 visibly states Article 10: cultivation of the cannabis plant is prohibited except Article 43, and Article 12 allows relevant controlled-substance operations only with express authorization and where use is limited to medical or scientific purposes. Page 12 visibly states Article 47: unauthorized culture, production, extraction, preparation or transformation of drugs is punishable by 10 to 30 years imprisonment and a large fine, and begins Article 49 for unauthorized offer, sale, distribution, holding, illicit use, purchase, delivery, shipment, transport, brokerage or other intermediation outside authorized scope. Page 13 visibly continues a maximum 30-year imprisonment penalty and Article 50's five-year penalty for illicit offering/ceding drugs for personal consumption. Page 15 visibly states Article 63: low-quantity illicit culture, purchase or holding for personal consumption is punishable by six months imprisonment and a fine, or one of those penalties, and the court may substitute or add detox/treatment. The 1975 decree was also rendered; page 3 visibly lists Cannabis (TTC), flowering/fruiting tops, leaves and resin as narcotics, and page 4 visibly prohibits unauthorized possession, manufacture/distribution, production encouragement and use in violation of the decree while recognizing licensed medical/scientific use. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported, with a personal-use treatment/sentencing caveat. Project medical=NONE is retained as programme-level status because the reviewed sources show only general controlled-substance authorization/medical-scientific exceptions, not a separate medical cannabis patient-access scheme. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Iraq is visually verified from the Iraqi Ministry of Justice-hosted Official Gazette PDF for issue 4446 containing Law No. 50 of 2017 on Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances. rows.differenceDescription: Kuwait is visually verified from official Kuwait Government Online and Ministry of Interior pages. The Kuwait Government Online screenshot visibly identifies the current Amiri decree-law No. 59 of 2025 on combating drugs and psychotropic substances and regulating their use and trafficking, states it is implemented two weeks after publication in the Official Gazette, and visibly states Article 83 repeals Law No. 74 of 1983 on combating drugs and Law No. 48 of 1987 on psychotropic substances. The same KGO screenshot visibly describes prohibitions or licensing controls around production, manufacture, import, export, transport, possession, purchase, sale, trafficking, dispensing, administration and cultivation of narcotic or psychotropic substances, and strict penalties including death or life imprisonment and large fines for trafficking/production/cultivation-for-trafficking. The Ministry of Interior screenshot visually shows an official drugs page citing Law No. 74 of 1983 Articles 33, 34 and 35, with Article 33 penalizing bringing, possessing, buying, producing or cultivating narcotic substances/plants for personal use unless licensed under law; a separate MOI screenshot visibly identifies Indian cannabis, hashish or marijuana and Cannabis Sativa. Because KGO shows Law 74/1983 was superseded by the 2025 decree, the MOI cannabis page is accepted as an official cannabis-specific government page with a superseded-law caveat, not as proof that Law 74 remains the current statute. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported. Project medical=NONE is retained as a cannabis patient-program status because the reviewed current material shows controlled medical prescriptions, licensing and rehabilitation/treatment provisions, not a regulated cannabis patient-access programme. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Kyrgyzstan is visually verified from the Kyrgyz Ministry of Justice centralized legal information bank (CBD) official API/rendered law content. The official frontend was WAF-protected during capture, so the accepted screenshots are local renders of official CBD API content with the frontend and API URLs shown in the header, analogous to rendering an official downloaded law document for visual inspection. The controlled-list screenshot visibly lists cannabis oil, cannabis resin/hashish, cannabis straw, cannabis straw concentrate/marihuana, extracts and tinctures. The size-criteria screenshots visibly list cannabis oil, cannabis resin/hashish, cannabis straw, cannabis straw concentrate/marihuana, extracts/tinctures and Cannabis (hemp), including thresholds such as Cannabis (hemp) 80 / 80-2400 / 2400. The Criminal Code current edition screenshot visibly shows Chapter 36 and Articles 282 and 283 punishing illegal narcotic-drug/psychotropic-substance/analogue sale scope and large non-sale scope with imprisonment/fine bands. Law No. 69 of 2024 screenshots visibly show the narcotic-drugs law title, prescription acquisition of medicines containing narcotic drugs/psychotropic substances in pharmacies, enforcement bodies, destruction of wild living organisms containing narcotic drugs/psychotropic substances, and confiscation. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported. Project medical=NONE is retained as a cannabis patient-program status because reviewed sources show general narcotic-medicine prescription/dispensing caveats, not a regulated cannabis patient-access programme. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Liberia is visually reviewed from official Executive Mansion and Ministry of Justice sources, but no live official direct cannabis-specific statutory text was confirmed in this pass. The Executive Mansion screenshot visibly states President Weah signed the Control Drug and Substance Act of 2023 into law, describes the Act as regulating/restricting/controlling/eradicating illegal narcotic substances, and visibly describes penalties for unlicensed import and manufacture of controlled drugs or substances, including non-bailable drug offenses and 10-to-20-year penalty bands. The Ministry of Justice 2015 Annual Report PDF was downloaded from moj.gov.lr and rendered locally; screenshots visibly state that passage of the Drug/Controlled Substance Act in 2014 created the legal framework for investigation/apprehension/prosecution/sentencing, that LDEA arrested 115 persons in violation of the Controlled Drugs and Substance Law and seized 5,112.7 kg of marijuana, and that specific marijuana trafficking/possession cases were charged and processed to court. Additional screenshots visibly show marijuana as the leading seized drug, major marijuana farming/cultivation activities, marijuana farms burned and plants seized, and implementation challenges around the Controlled Drugs and Substance Act of 2014. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT as official context. The reviewed official material does not show a medical cannabis patient-access program, so project medical=NONE is not contradicted. Because the direct cannabis-specific statutory schedule/text was not live-confirmed from an official host, the row is kept context-only rather than treated as a direct law page. No project status SSOT was changed.

legalInterpretation.notes: Maldives is visually reviewed from official Prosecutor General Office, President Office and Drug Court sources, but a live official-hosted direct Drugs Act No. 17/2011 statute text/PDF with cannabis provisions was not confirmed in this pass. The PGO screenshot/readable extract visibly lists Drugs Act No. 17/2011 cannabis trafficking charges under Article 108, Schedule 1 drug-use charges under Articles 111/116, a case including 139 grams of cannabis, and cannabis-use charges under Article 115. The President Office screenshot visibly states the President ratified the Third Amendment to the Drugs Act (Act No. 17/2011), that penalties for trafficking Schedule 1 drugs were increased, and that the death penalty may apply where trafficked Schedule 1 drug quantity exceeds 350 grams of cannabis at entry. The Drug Court screenshot visibly states the Drug Court is established under Act No. 17/2011 (Drug Act) for criminal cases of drug dependent persons and mandatory treatment/rehabilitation programs. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT as official context, and does not contradict medical=NONE because no regulated cannabis patient-access program was shown. Because direct official cannabis statute text was not live-confirmed, the row is kept context-only. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: No separate Martinique-issued cannabis law page was found or treated as direct territorial law. Instead, the official scope and cannabis evidence was visually reviewed as French national law/public-health material applicable to Martinique. The Vie-publique official overseas territories screenshots visibly list Martinique among the overseas departments/regions and state that the Article 73 legislative-identity regime means national laws and regulations apply as of right in overseas departments/regions, with possible adaptations and exceptions for regalian matters. The Drogues.gouv official screenshot visibly states that narcotic classification means a substance cannot be freely used, produced, manufactured, imported, exported, transported, possessed, offered or sold, and that these acts are heavily sanctioned by law; another visible crop says French narcotics law represses illicit use and traffic. The Service-public and ANSM screenshots visibly show the narrow medical cannabis transition: the experiment ended on 31 December 2024, no new patient can enter since 27 March 2024, only already-included patients continue prescriptions/deliveries, and the transition lasts until three months after a forthcoming HAS opinion. The ANSM professionals page visibly covers trained prescriber/pharmacist requirements, the five indications, THC above 0.3 percent as narcotic medicines on secured prescription/storage, and flower initiation stopped. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=LIMITED and enforcement=STRICT are supported by this national-DROM scope. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Mauritania is visually verified from the UNODC SHERLOC official legislation database record and attached PDF for Loi No. 93-37 on repression of production, traffic and illicit use of narcotics and psychotropic substances, attributed on the UNODC record to Mauritania / Ministry of Justice. rows.differenceDescription: Mauritius is visually verified from the official Laws of Mauritius current Dangerous Drugs Act PDF and the official National Assembly Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act 2022. The current Act screenshots visibly define gandia as Cannabis Sativa L or Cannabis Indica plant parts, hashish/charras/chiras as resin obtained from the cannabis plant, Indian hemp as dried flowering or fruiting tops of the cannabis plant, and medicinal cannabis as a cannabis-plant product. Section 5 visibly prohibits cultivation of the cannabis plant. Section 6 visibly prohibits producing, manufacturing, distributing, transporting, possessing, supplying, transferring, purchasing, using, importing, exporting or transiting First Schedule plants/substances/preparations; the First Schedule visibly lists Cannabis/Gandia/Indian Hemp excluding medicinal cannabis and Cannabis Resin excluding medicinal cannabis. The current Act also visibly contains Part IIA - Medicinal Cannabis: authorised patient, authorised specialist/pharmacist, specific therapeutic conditions, lawful use/importation only under Part IIA, regional-hospital Medicinal Cannabis Therapeutic Committee, request/approval/prescription/dispensing/register/importation rules, Ministry/police supervision, and a foreign-patient possession exception; the Second Schedule visibly lists Medicinal cannabis. Therefore project recreational=ILLEGAL is supported, but project medical=NONE is contradicted and should be reviewed as LIMITED/REGULATED. Project enforcement=SOFT is partially supported only for personal-consumption drug users because Part IIIA and section 59B visibly allow rehabilitation in lieu of prosecution where there are no aggravating circumstances and the user is not a trafficker; cultivation, unauthorised possession/use/import/export and Part II/IIA contraventions remain offences. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: No separate Mayotte-issued cannabis law page was found or treated as direct territorial law. Instead, the official scope and cannabis evidence was visually reviewed as French national law/public-health material applicable to Mayotte. The official Vie-publique/DILA Guide de légistique screenshots visibly identify Mayotte among the Article 73 overseas collectivities, state that Mayotte is a single collectivity called Département de Mayotte exercising overseas department and region competences, and state that under Article 73 legislative identity, laws and regulations apply there as of right without a special mention; the same page states the Article 73 regime for Guadeloupe, Guyane, Martinique, La Réunion and, since 31 March 2011, Mayotte is that of metropolitan France, subject to adaptations. The Drogues.gouv official screenshot visibly states that narcotic classification means a drug cannot be freely used, produced, manufactured, imported, exported, transported, possessed, offered or sold, that these acts are heavily sanctioned by law, and that French narcotics law represses illicit use and traffic. The Service-public and ANSM screenshots visibly show the narrow medical cannabis transition: the experiment ended on 31 December 2024, no new patient can enter since 27 March 2024, only already-included patients continue prescriptions/deliveries, and the transition lasts until three months after a forthcoming HAS opinion. The ANSM professionals page visibly covers trained prescriber/pharmacist requirements, five indications, THC above 0.3 percent as narcotic medicines on secured prescription/storage, and flower initiation stopped. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=LIMITED and enforcement=STRICT are supported by this national-Article-73/Mayotte scope. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Mexico is visually verified from official Orden Jurídico Nacional current consolidated Ley General de Salud and Código Penal Federal PDFs plus the official Diario Oficial medical-cannabis regulation PDF. The Ley General de Salud screenshots visibly show Article 235 subjecting seeding, cultivation, harvesting, preparation, acquisition, possession, commerce, transport, prescription, supply, use and consumption of narcotics to the health-law framework and Secretaría de Salud authorization; Article 235 Bis requiring public policies to regulate medicinal use of pharmacological derivatives of cannabis sativa, indica and americana or marihuana, including THC, and national research/production; Article 245's industrial exception for cannabis derivatives with 1 percent or less THC and broad industrial uses; Articles 477-479 creating penalties for unauthorized non-commercial possession above the table context but no criminal action for a consumer or dependent person who possesses table amounts for strict personal consumption outside specified places, with Cannabis Sativa, Indica or Mariguana listed at 5 grams; and the SCJN Declaratoria General de Inconstitucionalidad 1/2018 invalidating the absolute administrative prohibition on Health Secretariat authorizations for cannabis and THC self-consumption with recreational purposes. The DOF regulation screenshots visibly establish the health-control regulation for production, research and medicinal use of cannabis and pharmacological derivatives, define cannabis and cannabis medicines, require permits for sowing/production for research/fabrication, and create special prescription, pharmacy/botica, patient registry, possession and international-travel rules for cannabis medicines. The Código Penal Federal screenshots visibly retain prison penalties for narcotics production/transport/traffic/supply/possession and marihuana cultivation, while stating marihuana sowing/cultivation/harvesting is not punishable when carried out for medical and scientific purposes under federal authorization. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL only with explicit self-consumption authorization and 5g no-prosecution caveats, supports medical=REGULATED, and supports enforcement=SOFT for strict personal-use threshold while retaining strict penalties for trafficking, supply, unauthorized cultivation and possession outside those caveats. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Moldova is visually verified from official legis.md LP201/2025 URL plus official Government of Moldova PDF packages for the adopted LP201/2025 drug-control law, the 2026 Ministry of Health controlled-substances tables, the industrial/horticultural hemp authorization regulation, and the Penal Code drug-offence amendments package. The legis.md live URL was captured but headless access showed Cloudflare verification, so the accepted visual law text comes from official gov.md PDF protocol pages for the same LP201/2025 package. The LP201 screenshots visibly define canabis as flowering or fruiting tops of the Cannabis genus and cannabis resin containing THC with psychoactive effect under narcotic/psychotropic control, and define industrial/horticultural hemp as Cannabis with THC not exceeding 0.3 percent, cultivated for industrial/horticultural/food/fibre/stem/seed/oil/biomass purposes while excluding medical, recreational or experimental use. rows.differenceDescription: Morocco is visually verified from official ANRAC-hosted Bulletin Officiel PDFs. Loi n° 13-21 page 1 visibly promulgates the law relative aux usages licites du cannabis, defines cannabis, cannabis plant, cannabis flowering/fruiting tops, cannabis resin, narcotic and industrial purpose, and Article 3 requires ANRAC authorization for cannabis cultivation, production, nurseries, seed/plant import/export, transformation, fabrication, transport, commercialization, product export and product import. Article 5 visibly limits cultivation/production authorization to quantities needed for medical, pharmaceutical and industrial products. Page 2 Article 6 visibly states that cultivation/production authorization for cannabis varieties whose THC content exceeds the regulatory threshold can be granted only for medical and pharmaceutical industries. Page 3 Article 17 visibly prohibits manufacturing products exceeding the THC threshold except medicinal and pharmaceutical products. Page 6 visibly gives ANRAC control/reporting functions and includes measures aimed at ending illicit cannabis uses. Page 9 Article 50 visibly applies Dahir n° 1-73-282 sanctions/security measures to unauthorized cannabis culture, production, transformation, fabrication, transport, commercialization, export/import and seeds/plants import, while Articles 51-55 add prison/fine/confiscation and doubled recidivism penalties for violations of the licensed framework. Décret n° 2-22-159 visibly implements Loi 13-21, limits cultivation/production authorization to Al Hoceima, Chefchaouen and Taounate, creates application/committee/ANRAC procedures, and sets stock/THC/traceability-related implementation rules. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=REGULATED and enforcement=STRICT with the caveat that the law creates licensed medical/pharmaceutical/industrial cannabis channels rather than general recreational legalization. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Mozambique is visually verified from an official Supreme Court of Mozambique PDF, Acórdão Proc. nº 31/2022-P. Page 1 visibly shows República de Moçambique / Tribunal Supremo and a criminal appeal summary for tráfico e consumo de estupefacientes, stating that possession of 232 bolinhas of cannabis sativa commits the small-quantity trafficking offence under Article 36 of Lei nº 3/97 of 13 March, and that Article 55 possession/consumption requires proof that the drug was sufficient for three days of personal consumption. Page 6 visibly states that laboratory testing was positive for cannabis sativa, that the 590g substance falls within Table I-C annexed to Lei nº 3/97, and that commercialization of cannabis sativa was prohibited and criminally punishable. Page 7 visibly quotes Article 33 of Lei nº 3/97, punishing unauthorized cultivation, production, fabrication, extraction, preparation, sale, distribution, purchase, transfer, transport, import, export or illicit possession outside Article 55 of listed plants/substances with 16 to 20 years major imprisonment; the same page quotes Article 55, punishing consumption or own-use acquisition/possession of listed plants/substances with up to two years imprisonment and a corresponding fine. Page 10 visibly applies Article 36 small-quantity trafficking to 590g cannabis sativa with an abstract penalty range of 2 to 8 years major imprisonment and fine. Page 11 visibly states that although cannabis sativa is a so-called soft drug, in Mozambique its consumption continues to be absolutely prohibited and trafficking is more gravely censured. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT with a small-quantity-trafficking classification caveat. Reviewed official sources did not visually confirm any cannabis medical patient program, so project medical=NONE is not contradicted. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Myanmar is visually verified from the official Myanmar Trade Portal PDF of The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Law, Law No. 1/93, English version. Page 1 visibly shows the law title and defines Narcotic Drug to include cannabis plant, and defines production to include transforming cannabis plant into a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance. Page 6 visibly places offences and penalties in Chapter VIII, punishing a drug user who fails to register or follow medical-treatment directives with 3 to 5 years, and punishing cultivation of cannabis plant plus possession, transportation, transmission and transfer of narcotic drugs with 5 to 10 years and a fine. Page 7 visibly shows Section 19 punishing sale-purpose possession/transport/transfer and market communications for narcotic drugs with 10 years to an unlimited period. Page 8 visibly shows Section 20 punishing production, distribution, sale, import and export of narcotic drugs with 15 years to an unlimited period or death. Page 9 visibly shows Section 26 deeming possession/transport/transmission/transfer at the listed threshold, including cannabis or essence of cannabis, to be for sale purposes. Page 10 visibly creates general ministry-consent exclusions for production/research/medical-treatment use, possession, transport, sale, import/export, and Ministry of Health-permitted use, possession and transportation under a registered medical practitioner. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT. Project medical=NONE is not contradicted as a cannabis-patient-program status, but needs the general research/medical-treatment permission caveat. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Nigeria is visually verified from UNODC CLD official legal-database material. A Nigeria-government-hosted direct law page was not found in this pass, so the UNODC source-scope caveat remains visible. The Indian Hemp Act title page visibly identifies Chapter 16 Indian Hemp Act and states the Act makes planting, cultivation, importation and related acts involving Indian hemp offences. Page 2 visibly defines Indian hemp as any plant or part of a plant of the genus cannabis, separated resin from any plant of the genus cannabis, and preparations containing such resin. The same page visibly makes planting or cultivating any plant of the genus cannabis punishable by death or imprisonment for not less than twenty-one years, and import/sale/export punishable by not less than twenty-one years, with a medical-preparation exception for import/sale where no Dangerous Drugs Act offence is committed. Page 3 visibly continues Section 5: smoking Indian hemp or knowingly possessing Indian hemp is punishable by not less than four years without the option of a fine, with a medical-preparation exception for possession; it also punishes utensils and premises offences. Page 4 visibly contains supplementary jurisdiction/caning provisions for offenders under the Act. The NDLEA Decree No. 48 page 13 visibly covers cultivation of cannabis plant for narcotic-drug production in Section 11. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT. Project medical=NONE is retained as programme-level status because the reviewed texts show only medical-preparation exceptions / Dangerous Drugs Act caveats, not a regulated cannabis patient-access programme. No project status SSOT was changed.

Current map RED is not changed; SSOT, runtime, production and deployment remain unchanged. Повторный аудит: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает KP жёлтым композитным, а не одиночным источником. Актуальная UN Treaty Collection визуально показывает Democratic People's Republic of Korea стороной amended Single Convention с 19 March 2007. Официальный текст UNODC самой Convention визуально определяет Cannabis, Cannabis plant и Cannabis resin, определяет drug через Schedules I и II и в Article 4 обязывает стороны реализовать Convention на своей территории и ограничить производство, оборот, use и possession drugs исключительно medical and scientific purposes. independentTruth.conclusion: Applicable Palau National Code §3302(c)(1) makes possession of two ounces or less of marijuana a $500 citation payable within 30 days, with a $1,000 citation for a subsequent such violation; imprisonment begins only above that threshold. The same current Code retains general possession and trafficking prohibitions, places Marijuana in Schedule I under criteria requiring no accepted medical use/safety, and supplies no cannabis-specific patient eligibility, prescribing, dispensing, pharmacy, import or operational-programme proof. The generic controlled-substance prescription wording in §3302(a) is not treated as a cannabis patient route.

rows.differenceDescription: Peru is visually verified from official gob.pe/SUSALUD and DIGEMID/MINSA hosted El Peruano PDFs. Law No. 30681 page 1 visibly regulates medicinal and therapeutic cannabis and derivatives, permits access exclusively for medicinal and therapeutic use, covers informed use, research, production, importation and commercialization exclusively for medicinal and therapeutic purposes, creates patient/operator registries and requires licenses. Law 30681 page 2 visibly modifies Penal Code Articles 296-A, 299 and 300: cultivation or commerce of marihuana/cannabis sativa remains punishable outside the license exception, own immediate possession is not punishable up to eight grams of marijuana, and registered medical-cannabis possession/supply is not punishable when necessary for treatment. Supreme Decree No. 004-2023-SA page 1 visibly approves the regulation for medicinal and therapeutic cannabis; page 3 cites Law 30681 and Law 31312 and describes exclusive medical/therapeutic access and authorized production/import/commercialization; page 4 confirms official publication endpoints and Article 1.2 exclusive medicinal/therapeutic access; page 5 defines cannabis, psychoactive cannabis and non-psychoactive cannabis; page 8 establishes licenses and cancellation/suspension grounds including diversion to illicit destinations. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and medical=REGULATED. Enforcement is treated as SOFT for personal possession because Article 299 visibly makes small own-immediate marijuana possession non-punishable, with an explicit caveat that commercial/cultivation conduct and irregular medical-license abuse remain criminally strict. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Philippines is visually verified from official Dangerous Drugs Board PDFs. RA 9165 page 1 visibly identifies Republic Act No. 9165, the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. Page 5 visibly defines Cannabis, commonly known as Marijuana or Indian Hemp, as Cannabis sativa L. and related varieties and forms including hashish, bhang, ganjab, marijuana, resin, extract and tincture. DDB's Updated Lists of Scheduled Controlled Substances page 2 visibly lists Cannabis and Cannabis resin, extracts and tinctures in Schedule 1. RA 9165 pages 12-13 visibly set marijuana resin/oil and marijuana possession thresholds with penalties ranging from twelve to twenty years through life imprisonment/fine bands depending on quantity. Page 14 visibly sets use penalties and states that marijuana cultivation/culture carries life imprisonment to death and a P500,000 to P10,000,000 fine, while allowing only medical laboratories and medical research centers to cultivate/culture marijuana for medical experiments, research, or creation of new medicine subject to Board guidelines. This supports project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT. Medical is retained as LIMITED because official material shows narrow legitimate-medical/research carve-outs, but no visually confirmed full patient medical cannabis program or regulated commercial medical cannabis market. No project status SSOT was changed.

officialContextLinks.title: Qatar Al Meezan - Law No. 9 of 1987 on Control and Regulation of Narcotic Drugs and Dangerous Psychotropic Substances
officialContextLinks.note: Official Qatari Legal Portal / Al Meezan page. Visual review confirms Law No. 9 of 1987 is in force and governs narcotic drugs and dangerous psychotropic substances. Article 2 permits import, export, production, manufacture, cultivation, possession, trafficking, buying, selling, delivery, medical dispensation and prescription of narcotic substances/plants only under the law's conditions. Article 15 allows possession only for personal use and strictly health reasons in physician-prescribed quantities and legitimate medical treatment. Articles 28-30 prohibit cultivation, possession and trade in listed prohibited plants except narrow scientific/research authorizations. Article 34 sets ten-to-twenty-year imprisonment and high fines for trafficking/import/export/production/cultivation offences and death or life imprisonment for recidivists. Article 37 sets two-to-five-year imprisonment and fines for illicit consumption/personal use unless permitted under the law. Law 9 is retained as generic NDDPS status/enforcement context because the captured page did not visibly name cannabis; Law 4 Article 17 is the direct cannabis-naming source.

officialContextLinks.note: Current French law applies to Saint-Barthelemy through LO6213-1 and the Public Health Code territorial provisions. Article L3421-1 retains illicit narcotics use as an offence; Article R5132-86 specifically prohibits cannabis operations but permits medicine-authorisation scope. Current official product data separately proves EPIDYOLEX cannabidiol is prescription-only, a limited pharmaceutical exception. The old controlled therapeutic-cannabis transition article ended no later than 31 March 2026 and cannot prove a current operational programme. No BL-specific patient eligibility, prescriber, registry, lawful supply, pharmacy/dispensary or import route is proved. Independent proposal-only color remains YELLOW, not GREEN or RED.

rows.differenceDescription: St Helena is visually verified from the official St Helena Government Drugs (Prevention of Misuse) Ordinance, 2003 PDF updated 01/03/2023. Page 3 visibly defines cannabis as any plant of the genus cannabis and defines cannabis resin. Page 26 visibly lists Cannabis and Cannabis resin in Schedule 1 Class B. Page 7 visibly makes possession of controlled drugs unlawful unless the person has an exempt product acquired from a specified lawful source, and sets Class B possession penalties of a fine or imprisonment for 7 years; intent-to-supply Class B exposure is a fine or imprisonment for 14 years. Page 8 visibly makes cultivation of any plant of the genus cannabis unlawful and sets a fine or imprisonment for 14 years; it also includes 2023 narrow exempt-product sale/import conditions and under-18 sale restrictions. Page 10 visibly includes smoking cannabis or cannabis resin among prohibited activities and sets Class B exposure of a fine or imprisonment for 14 years. Page 29 visibly shows the attached Drugs (Authorisation of Cultivation and Possession) Regulations 2009 allow cannabis cultivation/possession only where authorised by the Governor for police-training purposes. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=NONE and enforcement=STRICT are supported, with the caveat that the law now contains narrow exempt-product and police-training authorization carve-outs that do not amount to a medical cannabis patient programme. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: St. Kitts and Nevis is visually verified from official Law Commission PDFs. Cannabis Act, 2020 page 4 visibly establishes the Medicinal Cannabis Authority to regulate, monitor and control cultivation, supply, possession, production and use of medicinal cannabis. Page 8 visibly states the Act's object is lawful access to medicinal cannabis for qualifying medical conditions and a comprehensive licensing scheme, and establishes the Authority. Page 18 visibly authorizes medical-doctor prescribing and authorizes a patient with prescription, identification card and medical certificate to obtain, possess, store and use medicinal cannabis. Page 21 visibly provides patient/caregiver identification cards and authorizes patients/caregivers to obtain, possess, store, use or administer medicinal cannabis. Page 25 visibly shows licensed medicinal cannabis supply activities and penalties for supply without licence. The 2022 Licensing Regulations page 9 visibly authorizes and licences medicinal cannabis business operations including cultivation, products manufacturing, testing, dispensary, lounge, transport and research and development. The 2023 Drugs Amendment Act page 2 visibly states possession provisions do not apply to listed cannabis licence/faith/medical contexts and to a person possessing fifty-six grammes or less of cannabis or fifteen grammes or less of cannabis resin under storage/access conditions, with retention and fixed-penalty/community-service/default-imprisonment consequences. Page 3 visibly states cultivation provisions do not apply to Medicinal Cannabis Authority licence holders, Rastafari assembly cultivation, faith-based licence cultivation of five cannabis plants or less, or a person cultivating five cannabis plants or less in a secured private residence, also with retention and fixed-penalty/community-service/default-imprisonment consequences. Project recreational=ILLEGAL, medical=LIMITED and enforcement=STRICT therefore conflicts with the official evidence at least on medical=REGULATED and enforcement not uniformly STRICT for the small possession/cultivation carve-out scope. Adult-use commercial retail legalization was not visibly confirmed. No project status SSOT was changed.

Официальный отчёт префекта Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon визуально фиксирует пресечение местного оборота herbe и résine de cannabis; Sénat визуально подтверждает принцип применения французских законов и регламентов de plein droit в архипелаге вне узких местных компетенций. Service Public визуально показывает окончание переходного медицинского режима 31 марта 2026 и отсутствие новых пациентов с марта 2024; более поздний действующий пациентский доступ не подтверждён. directOfficialCannabisLawLinks.note: Independent proposal only: YELLOW. Samoa's current official Narcotics Act directly classifies cannabis preparations, cannabis resin/oil and THC as Class B narcotics; adult possession/use and cultivation are offences unless expressly licensed or exempt. The Act permits a licensed/prescribed narcotic route, and the official Law Reform Commission specifically records that Narcotics Regulation 1967 reg. 3 provides scope for an approved licensee to import medicinal marijuana. That is a limited lawful case-by-case medicinal route, not proof of a current patient registry, provider network, dispensing system, completed cannabis import, or operational programme. The current 2026 Customs page confirms unauthorised marijuana import remains prohibited. Therefore the honest color is YELLOW, not GREEN and not RED.

rows.differenceDescription: Senegal is visually verified from the official CENTIF Sénégal PDF of Loi 97-18 du 1er décembre 1997 portant Code des Drogues. The rendered official law page visibly prohibits cultivation of the cannabis plant throughout the national territory. The same law visibly prohibits use of controlled drugs outside medical prescription and orders seizure/confiscation/destruction. Article 109 visibly punishes illicit purchase, possession or cultivation of small quantities for personal consumption with 2 months to 1 year imprisonment and a fine equal to triple the value of seized drugs, and explicitly includes cannabis oil and other cannabis-plant derivatives in that block; it also allows possible dispensation or relief from execution of sentence for listed non-recidivist/minor/undertaking-not-to-repeat conditions. Articles 95-100 visibly set broader custodial ranges for cultivation/production/traffic/facilitation/offer contexts. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported, with the Article 109 dispensation caveat. Project medical=NONE is not contradicted by the reviewed source because no cannabis-specific medical patient-access programme was confirmed; the source only shows general controlled-drug medical-prescription framing and an express cannabis-cultivation ban. No project status SSOT was changed.

officialContextLinks.title: India Code - Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
officialContextLinks.note: Второй поиск закрыт по четырём официальным документам и восьми заново просмотренным релевантным страницам. India Code NDPS Act визуально действует на whole of India, определяет cannabis (hemp), charas/hashish oil/liquid hashish, ganja и cannabis plant, запрещает выращивание и операции/употребление кроме разрешённого режима и устанавливает section 20 penalties. Gazette of Pakistan Cannabis Control and Regulatory Authority Act 2024 визуально действует на whole of Pakistan, определяет cannabis/CBD/THC и создаёт национальную лицензируемую систему выращивания, производства и продажи для medicinal, industrial и иных public uses. Официальные документы India MEA и Pakistan MOFA визуально подтверждают, что Siachen севернее NJ 9842 остаётся недемаркированной зоной с противоположными позициями и военным присутствием. Поскольку claimant cannabis regimes дают разные медицинские выводы и ни один источник не устанавливает нейтрально единую юрисдикцию либо KAS lawgiver, единый официальный цвет KAS не выводится; строка остаётся серой, а оба режима показаны как claimant context.

rows.differenceDescription: India and Pakistan official materials establish competing claimant contexts for Siachen/Kashmir, not a neutral territorial lawgiver or a documented single cannabis regime for the complete KAS GEO. India and Pakistan cannabis statutes remain claimant-state context evidence. The general resolver permits colour only after direct complete territorial applicability or proven convergence plus applicability; that threshold is not met here. KAS remains UNKNOWN until direct territorial scope/applicability evidence is available. Повторный аудит: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает KAS жёлтым без выбора суверена. Официальный India Code NDPS Act визуально действует на всю India, определяет cannabis (hemp), запрещает выращивание, производство, владение, продажу, покупку, перевозку, употребление и потребление, но прямо сохраняет лицензируемое исключение для medical/scientific purposes; section 20 устанавливает cannabis-specific наказания. Действующий официальный Pakistan Code CNSA 1997 визуально определяет cannabis/hemp, charas/hashish oil, bhang/siddhi/ganja и cannabis plant; sections 4 и 6 запрещают выращивание, владение, производство, продажу, покупку и перевозку, кроме разрешённых medical/scientific/industrial purposes, а sections 5 и 9 устанавливают строгие сроки лишения свободы. Pakistan Cannabis Control and Regulatory Authority Act 2024 дополнительно создаёт регулируемую medicinal/industrial cannabis-систему. Документы India MEA и Pakistan MOFA подтверждают противоположные позиции по Siachen, поэтому суверен не выбирается. Для KAS применяется явно обозначенный консервативный общий знаменатель всех визуально проверенных claimant-режимов: recreational запрещён, medical/scientific доступ ограничен разрешительным режимом, enforcement строгий. Это даёт жёлтый цвет и не означает признания чьего-либо суверенитета или равенства национальных программ доступа.

rows.differenceDescription: Sint Maarten is visually verified from the official lokale regelgeving Opiumlandsverordening and the official Sint Maarten National Gazette 2019 No. 16. The Opiumlandsverordening visibly defines hennep as the flowering or fruiting tops or parts of cannabis plants, forbids cultivation of plants of the genus Cannabis, forbids hemp extracts and tinctures, and controls hemp, hemp resin and common hemp-resin preparations such as hashish, esrar, chiras and djamba, with medical/pharmacy/veterinary and ministerial-exemption caveats. The National Gazette visibly publishes the Inspectorate VSA Policy on Medicinal Cannabis and CBD products dated July 17, 2019. It states medicinal cannabis should be available in Sint Maarten, that the objective is to establish procedures for doctors and pharmacists to import, store, distribute, prescribe and dispense medicinal cannabis in a controlled and safe manner, and that patients should have legal access to affordable, high-quality safe medicinal cannabis. It further summarizes the legal framework requiring opium exemptions, import authorization, product registration/licensing, registered medical practitioners and authorized pharmacy channels. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported with the medical-exemption caveat. Project medical=NONE is contradicted by the official medicinal cannabis policy and legal-access framework. No project status SSOT was changed.

rows.differenceDescription: Current Chile Ministry of Foreign Affairs material confirms that the 1998 Agreement remains in force while official mixed cartography and the Section B tracing work remain in execution. Argentina and Chile cannabis materials prove only their separate national regimes. A claimant-regime intersection cannot create a territorial cannabis law, patient route, or color for SPI. The prior LIMITED_OR_MEDICAL/YELLOW verdict is superseded by the general disputed-GEO applicability rule; all claimant evidence remains preserved as context only. No project status SSOT was changed. Повторный аудит: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает SPI жёлтым без выбора стороны незавершённой границы. В аргентинской ветке действующая Ley 23.737 сохраняет наказание за владение, но официальный федеральный приговор 2025 года применяет Arriola и исключает наказание за частное личное владение без конкретного вреда третьим лицам; Ley 27.350 прямо создаёт регулируемый medical/scientific cannabis framework. В чилийской ветке действующая Ley 20.000 Article 8 прямо называет cannabis, наказывает неразрешённое выращивание, выделяет personal-use sanction scope и признаёт medical-treatment cultivation по рецепту врача; Decreto 404 отдельно запрещает операции с cannabis/resin/extracts/tinctures, сохраняя ISP-controlled research и human-use pharmaceutical scope. Chile Ministry of Foreign Affairs визуально подтверждает, что совместная картография Section B по Agreement 1998 ещё выполняется, поэтому суверен для всей SPI не выбирается. Консервативный общий знаменатель двух визуально проверенных claimant-режимов: рекреационный рынок не легализован, ограниченный/регулируемый медицинский путь существует, enforcement варьируется от мягкого personal-use carve-out до уголовного запрета. В трёхцветной модели это жёлтый; вывод не скрывает различия режимов и не признаёт суверенитет.

officialContextLinks.title: Lawphil - Presidential Decree No. 1596 Kalayaan Island Group
officialContextLinks.note: Второй поиск исправляет прежнюю одностороннюю ветку Philippines. Официальный UN report A/47/623 визуально перечисляет шесть сторон Spratly: China, Taiwan and Viet Nam claim the whole archipelago; Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam and Philippines claim various atolls. Заново просмотрены официальные CannabisLawPages всех шести: Brunei Cap.27 относит cannabis/resin к Class A и запрещает possession/trafficking; China Criminal Law прямо называет marijuana и строгие уголовные санкции; Malaysia Act 234 определяет cannabis и предусматривает вплоть до life/death для trafficking; Philippines RA 9165 определяет cannabis и допускает лишь research/medical-experiment carve-out; Taiwan FDA прямо отвечает, что cannabis незаконен как Category II drug; Vietnam Decree 28/2026 включает cannabis plant/preparations в List I, а Law 73/2021 определяет cây cần sa и контролируемые/запрещённые операции. Claimant regimes дают неодинаковые медицинские и цветовые выводы, а PGA не является единым законодателем. Поэтому whole-Spratly строка остаётся серой с шестью явными ветками, а не получает цвет выбранного claimant.

rows.differenceDescription: Нейтральный PCA Award не решает суверенитет над Spratly Islands и не делимитирует границы. Источники China, Taiwan, Viet Nam, Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam и Philippines сохраняют cannabis-law факты своих claimant-режимов, но не создают единый PGA-issued закон и не доказывают применимость полного режима ко всему составному полигону. Общий resolver допускает colour при доказанном complete convergence и applicability; эти условия в данной записи не закрыты. PGA остаётся UNKNOWN до прямого территориального scope/applicability evidence. Повторный аудит: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает PGA красным без выбора суверена и без выдумывания единого закона Spratly Islands. Официальный UN report A/47/623 визуально перечисляет шесть claimant-веток: China, Taiwan и Viet Nam заявляют весь архипелаг, а Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam и Philippines — отдельные атоллы. Для каждой ветки заново просмотрена реальная официальная CannabisLawPage: Brunei Cap.27 относит cannabis и cannabis resin к Class A и запрещает неразрешённые possession, consumption, trafficking, manufacture и import/export; China Criminal Law Articles 347, 348, 351 и 357 прямо называют marijuana и устанавливают уголовные наказания; Malaysia Act 234 определяет cannabis, запрещает владение без authorisation и строго наказывает trafficking; Philippines RA 9165 определяет marijuana/Indian hemp, наказывает использование и выращивание, оставляя только medical-experiment/research carve-out; Taiwan FDA визуально называет cannabis незаконным Category II narcotic; Vietnam Decree 28/2026 помещает cannabis plant и preparations в List I, запрещённый для медицинского и социального использования вне специального research/testing/forensic/security режима, а Law 73/2021 прямо определяет cây cần sa и запрещённые операции. Исключения для разрешённой науки, экспериментов или контролируемых целей различаются и не образуют общего пациентского доступа для всей PGA. Поэтому явно обозначенный консервативный общий знаменатель всех шести визуально проверенных claimant-режимов — recreational запрещён, territory-wide medical patient access отсутствует, уголовный enforcement строгий. В трёхцветной модели это красный; вывод не отрицает отдельные национальные исключения и не признаёт чей-либо суверенитет.

independentTruth.conclusion: SJ is a composite GEO. Norwegian criminal law applies to both Svalbard and Jan Mayen, so the current national prohibition context reaches recreational axes in both components. The current health-law regulation expressly applies the Medicines Act and Pharmacy Act to Svalbard, while its exhaustive Jan Mayen section omits both. The current DMP cannabis protocol proves an operational named-patient, prescriber, pharmacy-delivery, and import route only where the medicines framework applies, therefore on Svalbard. It cannot be presumed to apply to Jan Mayen. The old conservative-intersection Red discarded this proven component divergence, which is forbidden by the general composite resolver. The only honest color for a combined GEO without a single unitary regime is unpainted UNKNOWN.

supplementalOfficialLinks.title: Правительство Норвегии — применимость права к Svalbard и Jan Mayen

rows.differenceDescription: The baseline collapsed component-specific medical applicability into a restrictive common color. Independent review proves Svalbard and Jan Mayen have different color-determinative medical axes, so the combined GEO is UNKNOWN proposal-only. No SSOT, map, runtime, production, or color application changed. Повторный аудит: Свежая визуальная перепроверка закрывает объединённый GEO SJ красным без переноса более благоприятного режима только одной физической части. Lov om Jan Mayen §§1–2 визуально подтверждает, что Jan Mayen является частью Kingdom of Norway и что норвежское уголовное право действует там прямо. Правительственный разбор Svalbardloven отдельно визуально подтверждает действие норвежского уголовного права на Svalbard. Действующий правительственный cannabis-раздел прямо объясняет, что оборот наркотиков допускается только для медицинских и научных целей, лечение cannabis регулируется отдельно, а иные dealing, use и possession уголовно наказуемы. Norwegian Medical Products Agency визуально подтверждает ограниченный пациентский путь через Sativex, Epidyolex и named-patient permits. Однако Forskrift 747 §11 прямо распространяет legemiddelloven и apotekloven на Svalbard, тогда как визуально проверенный исчерпывающий §18 для Jan Mayen их не перечисляет. Поэтому recreational prohibition и criminal enforcement доказаны для обеих частей, а ограниченный cannabis-patient pathway — только для Svalbard. По явно обозначенному консервативному общему знаменателю composite GEO получает красный: единого подтверждённого medical-cannabis access, общего для обеих частей, нет. Это не утверждение, что на Jan Mayen отсутствует любая медицинская помощь; это минимальный доказанный общий цвет объединённой ISO-строки.

directOfficialCannabisLawLinks.note: Law No.2/1993, официально переданный Government of Syria в UN, визуально показывает medical prescription, patient possession и ministerial authorization framework для narcotic medicines и отдельный запрет выращивания Schedule 4 plants. Свежая SANA визуально показывает задержание за выращивание القنّب для производства narcotic hashish, а SANA 2026 подтверждает продолжающее действие Law No.2/1993. Это жёлтый только как общий разрешительно-рецептурный режим для narcotic medicines; конкретный cannabis medicine и его фактическая доступность не доказаны.

rows.differenceDescription: Tanzania is visually verified from official National Prosecution Service and Parliament PDFs. The Act visibly defines cannabis, cannabis plant, cannabis resin and medicinal cannabis; treats cannabis plant as a prohibited plant; prohibits cultivation/dealing and trafficking/possession/use; and schedules cannabis, cannabis resin, extracts and tinctures. Enforcement is strict: Section 11 imposes imprisonment of not less than thirty years for cultivation/dealing with prohibited plants, Section 15 imposes life imprisonment for trafficking, Section 16 applies not less than thirty years to lesser trafficking quantities including cannabis/khat thresholds, and Section 18 still penalizes small-quantity personal use. Project recreational=ILLEGAL and enforcement=STRICT are supported. Project medical=NONE is kept with a caveat: the Act defines medicinal cannabis and Section 69 contains medical-necessity supply language for treatment centres/addicts and others, but no operating cannabis-specific patient access program was visually confirmed in the direct official evidence. No project status SSOT was changed.

independentTruth.conclusion: Tennessee has an enacted, narrow cannabidiol-oil exception below 0.9% THC with statutory documentation conditions. The Medical Cannabis Commission is current and extended, but its enabling text expressly says it does not authorize a medical cannabis programme or licences without later legislation; the 2025 Commission report asks for future legislation to establish such a programme. The Commission is therefore not patient access, and the exception is not a dispensary programme. Yellow follows from the narrow cannabis-related exception only.

independentTruth.conclusion: Law 7557 is a current primary statute. It expressly makes Health Ministry licensing or tracking-system registration available for cannabis-derived medical products and confines sales to pharmacies. That is a real limited lawful cannabis-derived medical-product regime, therefore Yellow. The statute delegates detailed permission and sales procedures to regulation, and available official sources do not identify an approved product, patient eligibility, prescriber route, actual lawful supply, or dispensing record. It therefore cannot meet Green. Non-medical cannabis-resin activities remain prohibited in Law 2313, but current personal-possession Penal Code text was inaccessible and is not invented. This route precludes a full Red conclusion regardless.

independentTruth.conclusion: Current official UAE materials support a general prohibition context for unauthorised recreational narcotic conduct, but they expressly reserve regulated medical or scientific activity. A new Federal Decree-Law No. 24 of 2025 on industrial and medical uses of industrial hemp is current from 2026-01-01. Its operative medical-scope clauses could not be read from the official primary-law source through HTTP, browser, or archive. The available regulator services are generic and do not identify cannabis medicines, patient eligibility, clinical authorization, or patient supply. Industrial hemp and generic controlled-drug import cannot create Green or Yellow; the unresolved current medical exception makes Red unprovable. Therefore the independent proposal is unpainted UNKNOWN, not a change to any production layer.
